source.text: וְאֶל־מֹשֶׁ֨ה אָמַ֜ר עֲלֵ֣ה אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹן֙ נָדָ֣ב וַאֲבִיה֔וּא וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם מֵרָחֹֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Moses he said, come up to Yahweh, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of [the] elders of Israel, and you will bow down from a distance.

en.L: And to Moses {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and you shall bow down from afar.
en.B: God also told Moses, "Come up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders. You are to bow low in worship while still far off.
en.R: God told Moses, "Come up the mountain to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Bring Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's leaders. You are to bow down and worship while you are still far away.

decisions.choice: he said: God speaks, giving a command that is carried out in verses 9-11
decisions.reason: The speaker is God, whose words from 20:22 to 23:33 have just ended. The command picks up 19:24, where Moses was told to come up with Aaron. It is set aside while the covenant is made (verses 3-8) and carried out in verses 9-11. God speaks of himself by name: "come up to Yahweh".

decisions.choice: bow down from afar: worship by bowing low, at a distance
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow to the ground, the act of worship. "From afar" sets the limit: these leaders worship at a distance, while Moses alone comes near (verse 2).

decisions.choice: Nadab and Abihu: Aaron's two eldest sons
decisions.reason: They are Aaron's first two sons (6:23), later ordained as priests with him (28:1). They die for offering unauthorized fire before Yahweh (Leviticus 10:1-2).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said". Balanced and Readable name God, since a new section begins. Readable also adds "the mountain" and "worship" to make the scene plain.

source.text: וְנִגַּ֨שׁ מֹשֶׁ֤ה לְבַדּוֹ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵ֖ם לֹ֣א יִגָּ֑שׁוּ וְהָעָ֕ם לֹ֥א יַעֲל֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will draw near Moses alone to Yahweh, but they not will draw near, and the people not will come up with him.

en.L: And Moses alone shall draw near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but they shall not draw near, and the people shall not come up with him."
en.B: Moses by himself is to approach {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The rest are to stay back, and the people are not to climb the mountain with him."
en.R: Only Moses may come close to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The others must keep their distance, and the people may not go up the mountain with him."

decisions.choice: Moses alone draws near: three degrees of nearness to God
decisions.reason: The people stay at the foot of the mountain (19:12, 21-24), the leaders worship partway up and from afar, and Moses alone comes near. The same order of nearness shapes the tabernacle, with its courtyard, holy place and most holy place (26:33-34; 27:9).

decisions.choice: they ... with him: the leaders of verse 1; him is Moses
decisions.reason: "They" are Aaron, his sons and the seventy elders; "him" is Moses.

decisions.choice: the mountain
decisions.reason: To "come up" is to climb Mount Sinai (19:12-13, 23-24). Balanced and Readable name the mountain.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר לָעָם֙ אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַן כָּל־הָעָ֜ם ק֤וֹל אֶחָד֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Moses and recounted to the people all [the] words of Yahweh and all the judgments, and answered all the people [with] one voice and said, all the words that has spoken Yahweh we will do.

en.L: And Moses came and recounted to the people all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and all the judgments. And all the people answered [with] one voice and said, "All the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken we will do."
en.B: Moses came and reported to the people all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said, every word and every rule. The whole people answered together as one: "We will do every word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken."
en.R: Moses went down and told the people everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said, including all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rules. All the people answered together, "We will do everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told us."

decisions.choice: the words and the judgments: the Ten Words and the case laws
decisions.reason: "The words" most likely means the Ten Words that God spoke to all the people (20:1-17), and perhaps all he said after them. "The judgments" are the rulings for particular cases introduced at 21:1, "These are the judgments", and running to 23:19.

decisions.choice: with one voice: all together, without dissent
decisions.reason: The whole people give the same answer at once, as they did in 19:8.

decisions.choice: all the words ... we will do: the people's pledge
decisions.reason: The people make the pledge three times: before the Ten Words (19:8), here, and again when the covenant is read and sealed (verse 7). Within weeks they break it with the golden calf (32:1-8).

decisions.choice: rule(s)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "judgments". Balanced and Readable say "rules": decisions for cases of law. Readable says "went down" for "came", since Moses returns from the mountain (19:24-25; 20:21).

source.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ תַּ֣חַת הָהָ֑ר וּשְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And wrote Moses all [the] words of Yahweh. And he rose early in the morning and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars for [the] twelve tribes of Israel.

en.L: And Moses wrote all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And he rose early in the morning and built an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
en.B: Moses put all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in writing. He was up early the next morning to build an altar below the mountain, with twelve pillars, one for each tribe of Israel.
en.R: Moses wrote down all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. Early the next morning he built an altar at the bottom of the mountain. Next to it he raised twelve pillars of stone, one for each tribe of Israel.

decisions.choice: pillars: standing stones set up as a witness or memorial
decisions.reason: These are upright stones, not the wooden pillars of the tabernacle. Such stones marked a meeting with God or witnessed an agreement (Genesis 28:18; 31:45-52; Joshua 4:20; 24:26-27). Here each stands for one tribe, so all Israel is present at the covenant.

decisions.choice: Moses wrote: the written record of the covenant
decisions.reason: What Moses writes here is the "book of the covenant" he reads to the people in verse 7. It is the first mention of Moses writing the law (compare 17:14; 34:27; Deuteronomy 31:9).

decisions.choice: under the mountain: at its foot
decisions.reason: "Under the mountain" means at its base, where the people were gathered (19:17; 32:19).

decisions.choice: pillars of stone
decisions.reason: Readable says the pillars were stone, so they are not confused with posts or columns of wood.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶֽת־נַעֲרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּֽעֲל֖וּ עֹלֹ֑ת וַֽיִּזְבְּח֞וּ זְבָחִ֧ים שְׁלָמִ֛ים לַיהוָ֖ה פָּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent the young men of [the] sons of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices, peace offerings to Yahweh, bulls.

en.L: And he sent the young men of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices [as] peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, bulls.
en.B: He sent out young men of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They presented burnt offerings and slaughtered bulls as fellowship offerings for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He sent some young Israelite men to make sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They offered burnt offerings and killed bulls for fellowship offerings.

decisions.choice: the young men: helpers chosen before there were priests
decisions.reason: No priests had yet been ordained; Aaron and his sons are set apart only in chapters 28-29. So Moses sends young men, perhaps for their strength in handling the animals, to offer the sacrifices.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings: the whole animal burned, and a sacrifice shared in a meal
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). The peace offering was a sacrifice of fellowship: part was burned, and the rest was eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:11-15). Such a meal may be the eating and drinking of verse 11.

decisions.choice: bulls: the animals offered
decisions.reason: "Bulls" stands last in the sentence. It names the animals of the peace offerings, and perhaps of both kinds of offering.

decisions.choice: fellowship offerings
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "peace offerings". Balanced and Readable say "fellowship offerings", the settled term, since the offering marks peace and fellowship with God.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ חֲצִ֣י הַדָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם בָּאַגָּנֹ֑ת וַחֲצִ֣י הַדָּ֔ם זָרַ֖ק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Moses half of the blood and put [it] in bowls, and half of the blood he threw on the altar.

en.L: And Moses took half of the blood and put [it] in bowls, and half of the blood he threw against the altar.
en.B: Moses kept half of the blood aside in bowls and dashed the rest against the altar.
en.R: Moses saved half of the blood in bowls. The other half he threw against the altar.

decisions.choice: threw: dashed or splashed, not sprinkled in drops
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw a liquid in quantity, the usual action with the blood of a sacrifice (29:16, 20; Leviticus 1:5, 11).

decisions.choice: half on the altar, half kept for the people: both parties bound by one blood
decisions.reason: The altar stands for God, and the rest of the blood is thrown on the people in verse 8. The same blood touches both sides of the covenant.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ סֵ֣פֶר הַבְּרִ֔ית וַיִּקְרָ֖א בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֥ה וְנִשְׁמָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took [the] book of the covenant and read [it] in [the] ears of the people, and they said, all that has spoken Yahweh we will do, and we will hear.

en.L: And he took the book of the covenant and read [it] in the ears of the people. And they said, "All that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken we will do, and we will hear."
en.B: Then he took the scroll of the covenant and read it aloud for the people to hear. They answered, "Whatever {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said, we will carry out. We will listen and obey."
en.R: He took the scroll of the covenant and read it out loud to the people. They answered, "We will listen to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and do all {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has told us."

decisions.choice: the book of the covenant: the written terms of the covenant, on a scroll
decisions.reason: The word means any written document; here it is the record Moses wrote in verse 4. Its contents are most likely God's words in 20:22-23:33, and perhaps the Ten Words. The phrase is used again of the law found in Josiah's day (2 Kings 23:2, 21).

decisions.choice: we will hear: listen and obey
decisions.reason: To "hear" God means to heed and obey him (19:5; Deuteronomy 6:4). Set after "we will do", it adds the people's promise to keep listening to what God says.

decisions.choice: read in the ears of the people: read aloud so all could hear
decisions.reason: As in 11:2, speaking "in the ears" of the people means speaking to them directly and aloud.

decisions.choice: the scroll of the covenant
decisions.reason: Books in Moses' day were written on scrolls, so Balanced and Readable say "scroll", as at 17:14. Literal keeps "book". Balanced and Readable say "obey" for "hear".

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וַיִּזְרֹ֖ק עַל־הָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה דַֽם־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם עַ֥ל כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Moses the blood and threw [it] on the people and said, look, [the] blood of the covenant that has cut Yahweh with you on all the words the these.

en.L: And Moses took the blood and threw [it] on the people and said, "Look, the blood of the covenant that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cut with you on [the terms of] all these words."
en.B: Moses took the blood and dashed it over the people. "Look," he said, "the blood of the covenant, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made with you on the terms of all these words."
en.R: Moses took the blood in the bowls and threw it on the people. He said, "This blood seals the covenant that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made with you. It rests on all these words."

decisions.choice: the blood of the covenant: the words Jesus takes up at the Last Supper
decisions.reason: Jesus says of the cup, "This is my blood of the covenant" (Mark 14:24; Matthew 26:28; compare Luke 22:20 and Zechariah 9:11). Hebrews 9:19-20 quotes Moses' words here and tells how he sprinkled the book and the people, adding water, scarlet wool and hyssop.

decisions.choice: cut a covenant: make a covenant
decisions.reason: The usual phrase for making a covenant is to "cut" it, probably from the animals cut in a covenant ceremony (Genesis 15:9-18; Jeremiah 34:18).

decisions.choice: blood on the people, on the terms of these words: the people bound to the covenant
decisions.reason: With half the blood on the altar (verse 6) and half on the people, both sides are joined in one covenant, whose terms are the words just read. Blood is used in the same way to consecrate the priests (29:20-21).

decisions.choice: in the bowls ... seals
decisions.reason: Readable says the blood was the half kept in the bowls (verse 6), and that it "seals" the covenant, to explain why Moses calls it "the blood of the covenant".

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן נָדָב֙ וַאֲבִיה֔וּא וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of [the] elders of Israel.

en.L: And Moses went up, and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
en.B: Moses then went up the mountain, with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
en.R: Then Moses climbed the mountain with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's leaders.

decisions.choice: went up: the command of verses 1-2 carried out
decisions.reason: Once the covenant has been sealed (verses 3-8), Moses and the leaders go up the mountain as God told them in verse 1.

decisions.choice: seventy of the elders: leaders standing for the whole people
decisions.reason: Seventy elders represent all Israel, as later in Numbers 11:16-25. Seventy is also the number of Jacob's family that went down to Egypt (1:5).

decisions.choice: the mountain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the mountain, Sinai, which they climb.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֕וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְתַ֣חַת רַגְלָ֗יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה֙ לִבְנַ֣ת הַסַּפִּ֔יר וּכְעֶ֥צֶם הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָטֹֽהַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they saw the God of Israel, and under his feet like [the] work of [the] pavement of the sapphire, and like [the] substance of the heavens for clearness.

en.L: And they saw the God of Israel, and under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet [was something] like a work of pavement of sapphire, and like the very heavens for clearness.
en.B: They saw the God of Israel. Beneath {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet there seemed to be a floor paved with sapphire, as pure and clear as the sky itself.
en.R: They saw the God of Israel. Under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet was what looked like a floor made of bright blue sapphire. It was as clear as the sky.

decisions.choice: they saw the God of Israel: a real but limited sight of God
decisions.reason: Later God tells Moses, "No one can see me and live" (33:20), and lets him see only his back (33:23). Here the text says the leaders saw God, yet it describes only what was under his feet. They saw a form of God's presence, as the prophets later did (Isaiah 6:1; Ezekiel 1:26-28), not God's full glory, which no one has seen (John 1:18; 1 Timothy 6:16). That they lived is the point of verse 11.

decisions.choice: sapphire: a deep blue precious stone, most likely lapis lazuli
decisions.reason: The stone named here was deep blue, the color of the sky. It was most likely lapis lazuli, a blue stone flecked with gold, widely prized in the ancient Near East; the clear gem now called sapphire was little known then. The same stone is under God's throne in Ezekiel 1:26.

decisions.choice: like the very heavens for clearness: as clear as the sky itself
decisions.reason: "The substance of the heavens" means the sky itself. The pavement was as pure and clear as a cloudless sky.

source.text: וְאֶל־אֲצִילֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֖ח יָד֑וֹ וַֽיֶּחֱזוּ֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And against the nobles of [the] sons of Israel not he sent his hand. And they beheld God, and they ate and they drank.

en.L: And against the nobles of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. And they beheld God, and they ate and drank.
en.B: Against the chief men of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not stretch out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. They gazed on God, and they ate and drank.
en.R: Even so, God did not harm these leaders of Israel. They looked at God, and they ate and drank a meal there.

decisions.choice: send his hand against: strike, do harm to
decisions.reason: To send or stretch out the hand against someone is to strike them (3:20; Genesis 22:12). The leaders saw God and were not struck down, though the people had been warned they would die if they broke through to look (19:21).

decisions.choice: they beheld God and ate and drank: a covenant meal in God's presence
decisions.reason: A different verb for seeing is used here, often used of seeing in a vision (Isaiah 1:1; Numbers 24:4). The leaders eat and drink before God, most likely the meat of the peace offerings (verse 5), a meal that seals the covenant (compare Genesis 31:54; Deuteronomy 27:7). See the note at verse 10 on seeing God.

decisions.choice: the nobles: the chief men, the leaders of verse 9
decisions.reason: The word means the leading or chief men; it refers to Aaron, his sons and the seventy elders.

decisions.choice: God did not harm
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says "did not harm" for "did not send his hand against". It also says "a meal" for the eating and drinking.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲלֵ֥ה אֵלַ֛י הָהָ֖רָה וֶהְיֵה־שָׁ֑ם וְאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת־לֻחֹ֣ת הָאֶ֗בֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה֙ וְהַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתַ֖בְתִּי לְהוֹרֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, come up to me to the mountain and be there, and I will give to you the tablets of the stone and the law and the commandment that I have written to teach them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Come up to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the mountain and be there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment which I have written to teach them."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Come up to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the mountain and remain there. I will give you the tablets of stone, the law and commandment that I have written to teach the people."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Come up the mountain to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and wait there. I will give you the stone tablets on which I have written {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching and commands, so the people can learn them."

decisions.choice: the tablets ... and the law and the commandment: the tablets, which hold the law and commandment
alternatives: the tablets of stone, together with the law and the commandment
decisions.reason: The "and" may explain what is on the tablets (the tablets, that is, the law and commandment written on them). Or it may add more teaching beyond the tablets, which Moses received during his forty days on the mountain (chapters 25-31).

decisions.choice: law: instruction, teaching
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction, God's direction for how his people are to live. "To teach them" at the end of the verse fits this sense.

decisions.choice: which I have written: written by God himself
decisions.reason: The tablets were "written with the finger of God" (31:18; 32:16). When they are broken, God writes the words again (34:1).

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: "Them" is the people of Israel; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable also joins the clauses to say what is written on the tablets.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם מֹשֶׁ֔ה וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ מְשָׁרְת֑וֹ וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Moses and Joshua his servant, and went up Moses to [the] mountain of God.

en.L: And Moses arose, and Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
en.B: Moses got up, along with Joshua who served him, and Moses climbed the mountain of God.
en.R: Moses and his helper Joshua got ready, and Moses went up God's mountain.

decisions.choice: servant: an attendant or aide, not a slave
decisions.reason: The word means one who serves or assists, a personal aide. Joshua is called this again in 33:11, Numbers 11:28 and Joshua 1:1. He first appears in 17:9, leading Israel against Amalek.

decisions.choice: Moses went up: Joshua goes only part of the way
decisions.reason: Moses is named again as the one who goes up, so Joshua seems to stay partway up the mountain. He is with Moses again when Moses comes down (32:17).

decisions.choice: the mountain of God: Sinai, also called Horeb
decisions.reason: Sinai is "the mountain of God" where God first met Moses at the burning bush (3:1; 4:27; 18:5).

source.text: וְאֶל־הַזְּקֵנִ֤ים אָמַר֙ שְׁבוּ־לָ֣נוּ בָזֶ֔ה עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־נָשׁ֖וּב אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַהֲרֹ֤ן וְחוּר֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם מִי־בַ֥עַל דְּבָרִ֖ים יִגַּ֥שׁ אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to the elders he said, remain for us in this [place] until that we return to you. And look, Aaron and Hur [are] with you; whoever [is] a master of matters, let him draw near to them.

en.L: And to the elders he said, "Stay for us in this [place] until we return to you. And look, Aaron and Hur [are] with you; whoever [is] a master of matters, let him draw near to them."
en.B: To the elders he said, "Remain here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur will be with you; if anyone has a case to settle, they can go to those two."
en.R: Moses said to the leaders, "Remain in this place until we return to you. Aaron and Hur will be with you. Anyone who needs a quarrel settled should go to them."

decisions.choice: a master of matters: someone with a case or dispute
decisions.reason: "Master of matters" means a person with a case to be judged. Moses had heard such cases himself, then shared the work with chosen judges (18:13-26). While he is away, Aaron and Hur are to settle them.

decisions.choice: Aaron and Hur: the two who held up Moses' hands
decisions.reason: Aaron and Hur held up Moses' hands in the battle against Amalek (17:10-12). A Hur is grandfather of Bezalel, the tabernacle craftsman (31:2), perhaps the same man.

decisions.choice: we: Moses and Joshua
decisions.reason: "We" are Moses and Joshua, who go up together (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: Readable names Moses as the speaker.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הָהָ֑ר וַיְכַ֥ס הֶעָנָ֖ן אֶת־הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Moses to the mountain, and covered the cloud the mountain.

en.L: And Moses went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
en.B: Moses climbed the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
en.R: Moses went on up the mountain, and the cloud hid the mountain from view.

decisions.choice: the cloud: the cloud of God's presence
decisions.reason: "The cloud" is the one already known, the cloud in which God came down on Sinai (19:9, 16) and in which he led Israel (13:21-22). It later covers the tent of meeting (40:34).

decisions.choice: hid the mountain from view
decisions.reason: Readable says the cloud "hid" the mountain to show what "covered" means here.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכֹּ֤ן כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה֙ עַל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וַיְכַסֵּ֥הוּ הֶעָנָ֖ן שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י מִתּ֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt [the] glory of Yahweh on Mount Sinai, and covered it the cloud six days. And he called to Moses on the day the seventh from [the] midst of the cloud.

en.L: And the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dwelt on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud.
en.B: The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to dwell on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered the mountain six days. On the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called to Moses from inside the cloud.
en.R: The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stayed on Mount Sinai. The cloud covered the mountain for six days. On the seventh day, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke from the cloud and called Moses.

decisions.choice: dwelt: settled and stayed
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle down and dwell. From the same root comes the word for the tabernacle, God's dwelling (25:8-9). The glory that dwells on Sinai will later fill the tabernacle (40:34-35).

decisions.choice: covered it: covered the mountain
decisions.reason: "It" is most likely the mountain, as in verse 15. It may instead be "him", Moses, who waited in the cloud six days before God spoke.

decisions.choice: six days ... the seventh day: the pattern of creation
decisions.reason: God speaks on the seventh day after six days of waiting, the pattern of the creation week (Genesis 1:1-2:3; 20:11). What God tells Moses after this also closes with the Sabbath (31:12-17).

decisions.choice: the mountain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the mountain for "it". Readable names "the LORD" for "he".

source.text: וּמַרְאֵה֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכֶ֖לֶת בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] appearance of [the] glory of Yahweh [was] like a fire devouring on [the] top of the mountain in [the] eyes of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And the appearance of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] like a devouring fire on the top of the mountain, in the eyes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: As the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} watched, the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared on the mountaintop like a fire that devours.
en.R: To the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} watching below, the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on top of the mountain looked like a fire that burns everything up.

decisions.choice: a devouring fire: a fire that consumes
decisions.reason: The fire "eats" whatever it touches. God himself is called "a devouring fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24; 9:3; Hebrews 12:29).

decisions.choice: in the eyes of the sons of Israel: as it looked to the people
decisions.reason: The verse tells how the glory looked to the people watching from the foot of the mountain, while Moses was inside the cloud.

decisions.choice: the glory as fire: God's presence both glorious and dangerous
decisions.reason: As at the burning bush (3:2) and when God came down on Sinai in fire (19:18), the fire shows God's holiness: it draws near, yet no one may approach it unbidden.

decisions.choice: watching below
decisions.reason: Readable says the people were below, watching, to make the point of view clear.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הֶעָנָ֖ן וַיַּ֣עַל אֶל־הָהָ֑ר וַיְהִ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ בָּהָ֔ר אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went Moses into [the] midst of the cloud and went up to the mountain. And was Moses on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

en.L: And Moses went into the midst of the cloud and went up to the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
en.B: Moses walked into the cloud and climbed the mountain, and there on the mountain he remained for forty days and forty nights.
en.R: Moses went into the cloud and kept climbing the mountain. He was there on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights: a long time alone with God
decisions.reason: Moses neither ate bread nor drank water in these forty days (Deuteronomy 9:9). Elijah travels forty days and nights to the same mountain (1 Kings 19:8), and Jesus fasts forty days and forty nights in the wilderness (Matthew 4:2).

decisions.choice: Moses was on the mountain: the setting of chapters 25-31
decisions.reason: God's instructions for the tabernacle and the priests (25:1-31:18) are given during these forty days. Meanwhile the people, tired of waiting, make the golden calf (32:1).
